einzeiler: How American universities lost their way and what it will take to fix them
kurzfassung: Peter Berkowitz joins the show to discuss the decline of liberal education in American universities and the rise of political indoctrination. The conversation traces the historical roots of illiberal trends from 1960s student activism and postmodern French philosophy to modern campus bureaucracy. Finally, the guests explore potential solutions, emphasizing the need for long-term reform across multiple fronts.
stichpunkte: Liberal education is essential for a free society by preparing citizens for the responsibilities of self-governance.
Universities have shifted away from open inquiry toward ideological indoctrination and political activism.
The intellectual roots of this shift trace back to 1960s campus radicals entering academia and the importation of French postmodernism.
Administrative growth and speech codes institutionalized these changes throughout the 1990s and 2000s.
High-profile controversies, including the fallout from Larry Summers' tenure at Harvard and reactions to October 7th, exposed deep institutional double standards.
Foreign funding from nations like Qatar and China has further distorted Middle Eastern and Asian studies programs.
Reforming higher education requires a multi-front approach, including new alternative colleges, civic thought programs, and foundational scholarship.

clips.hook: Postmodernism and the rejection of grand narratives
clips.text: The core message of influential French theorists was that everything remains open to interpretation and universal truths do not exist.

clips.hook: Student groups blaming Israel immediately after the attacks
clips.text: Dozens of student organizations at Harvard published statements placing full blame for the violence squarely on Israel.

clips.hook: The striking double standard in campus activism
clips.text: Massive casualties and displacement in neighboring conflicts failed to spark the widespread campus demonstrations seen regarding other regions.

clips.hook: John Stuart Mill on partial truths and debate
clips.text: Most moral and political viewpoints combine elements of truth and error, making open dialogue essential to separating the two.

clips.hook: Publishing nonsense to test academic peer review
clips.text: A mathematics professor successfully published a deliberately absurd paper filled with nonsensical equations in a prominent academic journal.

beschreibung:
Peter Berkowitz returns to the show to trace the slow collapse of liberal education in America, all in his new book, Reclaiming Liberal Education in America. In this episode, he and Eli Lake walk through 50 years of ideological capture, from the campus radicals of the 1960s who became the tenured professors of the 1980s, to the speech codes of the 1990s, to October 7, 2023, as the moment it all came into full view. Along the way, they dig into the French postmodernists who gutted academic standards, the DEI bureaucracies that replaced intellectual diversity with conformity, and the peer review process that failed so spectacularly. They end on the essential question: Can the university still reform itself, or is it time to build something new?
